thread.title: Islanders end season with 2-1 loss to Hurricanes at UBS Arena
thread.title_full: Islanders end season with 2-1 loss to Hurricanes at UBS Arena

author: y. r. walker
title: Islanders end season with 2-1 loss to Hurricanes at UBS Arena
text:
The New York Islanders concluded their season with a 2-1 defeat against the Carolina Hurricanes at UBS Arena on April 15. Bo Horvat scored the only goal for the Islanders, while Nikolaj Ehlers and Mark Jankowski found the net for Carolina. David Rittich made his first start since March 24 and recorded 19 saves, but Brandon Bussi stopped 28 shots to secure the win for the Hurricanes.
The result meant that the Islanders were swept in their season series against Carolina and missed out on playoff contention for a second consecutive year. The team finished with a record of 43-34-5, totaling 91 points—an improvement of nine points over last season’s tally.
Horvat reflected on the disappointment in missing their postseason goal: “Everybody sitting in here doesn’t like how this feels right now,” Horvat said. “It’s up to us this summer to get better, find ways to improve individually and collectively as a team. We don’t want to be sitting here feeling like this again next year.”
The game featured notable milestones and debuts. Victor Eklund made his National Hockey League debut, picking up his first career point by assisting on Horvat’s milestone goal—the center’s career 300th—which tied the game during the second period. Horvat insisted that Eklund keep the puck from his own achievement: “He’s going to have to fight me over it, because I’m not taking that puck,” Horvat said with a laugh. “It’s not only special to play in the NHL for your first game, but to get a point, you’ll never forget your first one. For me, obviously [300 goals] is special, but I definitely want him to have that.”
Eklund described his experience positively: “I had the best time of my life,” he said about playing in his first NHL game.
Other highlights included Foudy making his season debut after scoring a career-high with Bridgeport earlier in the year; Tony DeAngelo praised Foudy’s speed as complementing Casey Cizikas well on their line together: “He’s flying,” DeAngelo said of Foudy.
Matthew Schaefer attempted a team-high number of shots as he aimed for an NHL rookie defenseman record; Adam Pelech completed all games this regular season—a personal milestone after ten years in professional hockey—earning praise from teammates such as Horvat: “He was one of our key pieces back there this entire year…We needed him in the lineup every single night…”
In addition, fans participated alongside players during postgame traditions including “Jerseys Off Our Backs.” Reflecting on fan support throughout highs and lows this season, Horvat said: “They’re stuck with us…they showed up every single night…so we can’t thank them enough for their support this entire year.”
Looking ahead, players expressed optimism about future seasons thanks to emerging young talent within their ranks.
